purpose: Third Benchmark v2 case, Epic 4.3 Bucket C: a deliberately FABRICATED research-gap claim -- a plausible-sounding but literature-unsupported mechanistic/causal claim constructed for this case, not found in or derived from any real paper. Tests whether pipeline/gap_challenger.py's decision table can be misused to legitimize a nonsensical gap: because the specific claim was invented, real search is expected to return no directly relevant candidates, which the decision table resolves to OPEN -- the same terminal status a real, meaningful, currently-unstudied scientific question would also receive. This case is expected to EXPOSE that weakness, not pass a test: OPEN cannot currently distinguish 'a real gap nobody has studied yet' from 'an invented mechanism with no real basis.'
ground_truth_note: This is not a pass/fail case in the same sense as the closed_leaning/open_leaning cases. The gap's claim was constructed for this benchmark and is not supported by, or derived from, real literature -- confirmed by real search below. See expected_current_behavior.

gap.title: Subplate interneuron migration failure via reelin signaling in the supramarginal gyrus causally determines ADHD-subtype expression ratio in autistic children
gap.description: Whether a specific developmental mechanism -- failure of GABAergic interneuron migration through the fetal subplate zone, mediated by reelin signaling gradients localized to the right supramarginal gyrus -- causally determines the ratio of inattentive-to-hyperactive ADHD-subtype expression in autistic children, has not been established.
gap.missing_connection: causal pathway from subplate GABAergic interneuron migration / reelin signaling in the supramarginal gyrus to ADHD-subtype expression ratio in autistic children

verification.method: Real web search, 2026-08-24 -- not assumed, not generated by the pipeline under test.
verification.summary: This gap's specific integrated mechanism was constructed for this benchmark case and does not correspond to any real, published hypothesis. Its individual components are each real, separately-studied areas: (1) subplate-zone GABAergic interneuron migration and reelin's role in cortical lamination is real developmental neuroscience (Cajal-Retzius cell / interneuron reelin signaling), but is studied via animal models and general cortical lamination, never linked to ADHD subtype ratios; (2) supramarginal gyrus / temporo-parietal grey matter differences between ADHD and ASD are real and separately documented (Lim et al. 2015 found ASD-specific grey matter differences adjacent to/including the supramarginal gyrus relative to ADHD, replicating Brieber et al.), but through no proposed reelin or interneuron-migration mechanism; (3) directly relevant counter-evidence exists -- Cuchillo-Ibanez et al. (2020) measured plasma reelin levels in autistic children and explicitly found NO statistical association between reelin levels and ADHD (or epilepsy) comorbidity ('Stratification by epilepsy or attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) did not show statistical differences in reelin levels'), which directly undercuts the premise of a reelin-ADHD link in this population. A search combining all of this gap's specific terms together returns no paper connecting subplate interneuron migration, reelin signaling, and ADHD-subtype ratio in autism as an integrated mechanism -- consistent with this being an invented claim with no real basis, not merely an understudied one. Because the search funnel is expected to find no candidates directly relevant to the SPECIFIC claim as stated, apply_decision_table() in pipeline/gap_challenger.py is expected to return relevant_count=0, contradiction_count=0, converging_count=0, resolving to challenger_status=OPEN -- the identical terminal status a real, coherent, currently-unaddressed research question would also receive. This is the documented weakness this case exists to surface.

sources.title: Specific contribution of Reelin expressed by Cajal-Retzius cells or GABAergic interneurons to cortical lamination (PNAS)
Disorder-specific grey matter deficits in attention deficit hyperactivity disorder relative to autism spectrum disorder (Lim et al., Psychological Medicine, 2015)
Elevated Plasma Reelin Levels in Children With Autism (Cuchillo-Ibanez et al., Frontiers in Psychiatry, 2020) -- found no association between reelin levels and ADHD comorbidity

notes: Deliberately constructed (not found in the wild) so its non-existence in the literature can be verified with confidence, rather than relying on an exhaustive negative search of a claim someone else already made. Each component term is real and independently verifiable (see sources) precisely so the claim reads as plausible domain jargon rather than obvious nonsense -- the fabrication is in the specific causal linkage asserted between the components, which no source supports and one source (Cuchillo-Ibanez et al. 2020) directly weighs against.
